title: His father's ice house job and his mother's Algiers family
summary: Father worked as an ice pusher; mother was from Algiers and knew the Allen family; how they met and married.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What did your father do for a profession? What was his...

Well, he worked in an ice house. It was an ice, what you call an ice pusher. These are guys that, when the three or four hundred pounds of ice would come out in a block, it'd come down the chute, and he would catch it with the ice hooks and raise it up there and stack it and put it in the ice house
there in that packing place there. Must have been a big guy.
No, he was about 180 pounds, but he was strong. He was a strong man. He used to lift the 400 pounds of ice up,
just grab it on the chute and lift it right up. And what about your mother?

My mother, she came from Algiers, Louisiana. She was born in Algiers, Louisiana and all the family. And they knew the Red Allen, they knew the Allen family over there. She knew Red Allen and all the... his father and all the Allen family. And she used to speak of old man Allen. Yeah. And she used to tell us many things, but she was a housewife.
Yeah. And so where did they meet? How did your family, your folks meet?

I think my father went to Algiers over there to either see a baseball game or something happened over there that he was over there at that time and he met my mother. During that time, he used to have little dances, go on and things like that. So they met in Algiers and they married in New Orleans. They came over this time. After my grandmother died, my mother moved to New Orleans with her aunt. And that's when my father married my mother in New Orleans.
